title: The action of a finite family of increasing kernels preserves the stochastic order and stabilises the decreasing-density class
source_title: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

standard_prerequisites.name: Increasing kernel and stochastic order
standard_prerequisites.statement: A kernel is increasing when it preserves the order on measures; join(la; l_R) is the law obtained by applying the kernel l_R to la.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first assertion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Decreasing-density class
standard_prerequisites.statement: mdec(la) is the class of measures with decreasing density with respect to la.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the class that the second assertion shows is stabilised.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cumulative distribution functions
standard_prerequisites.statement: The order on measures is tested on cumulative distribution functions, which are affine on the components of A_r.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the argument of the second half of the proof.

core_obligations: For each r, check that the elementary kernel l_r is increasing and stabilises the decreasing-density class, which gives the first assertion and the first part of the second, since l_R only depends on the family (A_r) for r in R (source lines 1532-1533).
For mu in mdec(la), compare mu with mu applied to l_R through their cumulative distribution functions (source line 1533).

Observe that the two cumulative distribution functions coincide off the components of A_r, and that on each such component the one of mu applied to l_R is affine while the one of mu is concave because mu has decreasing density, so the inequality follows (source line 1533).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the elementary kernels l_r.
Compare cumulative distribution functions and use concavity on each component.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.4 at source lines 1519-1530: for a finite set R and measures mu, nu in a class of measures, if mu <= nu then mu applied to the kernel l_R is again <= nu applied to it, and if mu has decreasing density then so does mu applied to l_R with mu <= that measure. The author's proof (source lines 1532-1533) is short but contains two different arguments: the first assertion and the first half of the second are reduced to the elementary kernels l_r, for which increase and stabilisation are checked directly (line 1532), while the inequality mu <= mu applied to l_R is proved by passing to cumulative distribution functions, noting that they agree off the components of A_r and that on each component one is affine and the other concave precisely because mu has decreasing density (line 1533). The statement is a two-part lemma about kernels and records neither the reduction to the l_r nor the concavity argument.
